title: Coil and hang a rope on a wall hook
instruction: Coil the rope lying on the table into a loop and hang it on the wall hook so the coil hangs freely with no rope touching the table.
context: Rope coiling and stowing is a routine task in construction, warehouses, and marine settings. Keeping ropes organized and off the floor prevents trip hazards and equipment damage.
setup: One brown braided-nylon rope (120 cm long, 12 mm diameter, ~130 g) lies loosely and uncrossed on a wooden table (120 x 80 x 4 cm). A steel J-hook (40 mm projection, 10 mm diameter rod, silver) is mounted on a grey panel 40 cm above and 30 cm behind the table's far edge. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers face the table. The fixed layout is shown in the screenshot.
scoring: 0.25 if the rope is lifted fully off the table for one continuous second with both grippers holding it; 0.5 if the rope is coiled with all segments within 15 cm of the coil centroid; 1.0 if the coil hangs on the hook for five continuous seconds with no rope touching the table and both grippers released. All other outcomes score 0.
run_limit: 3000 steps (150 seconds at 20 Hz), including the five-second hang check.
reset_notes: Uncoil the rope and restore the flat uncrossed layout on the table.
fidelity: 20 joined capsules approximate braided nylon; grasping uses physical contact with no endpoint forces assisting coiling. Mass follows a commercial 12 mm rope; friction and bending stiffness are uncalibrated. Fibres, stretch and wear are omitted. Physics runs at 240 Hz; control stays at 20 Hz.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0. Both independently replayed.
